title: Lessons with Vic Lebowski and the legitimate pianists
summary: Hug studied with technician Vic Lebowski and discusses other legitimate pianists.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Do I remember Vic Lebowski? Oh, I took lessons from Vic. After I left Mrs. Asap, as I told you, I began just going out on my own, you know, and learning the jazz tunes and learning how to play jazz. But then after a couple of years I realized that I should improve a little bit on my technique and knowledge of music. So I started taking lessons from Vic, and I took about six months from him, and he really helped me quite a lot. But I never, I just couldn't get away from the unorthodox playing. In fact, Vic used to laugh at a lot of things that I do. He'd say, I don't understand how you can do that. He said, you're doing it all wrong, but somehow or another it comes out. And I think that's a good point to bring out in jazz right here, Vic, is the fact that jazz musicians did in those days unorthodox things that came out real good. And in fact, Vic's, you know, played a lot of things that were unorthodox, but they came out so, so wonderful. And I guess Louis Armstrong and all the old trumpet players and old musicians, in fact, we know Rapola must have done a lot of unorthodox things, but they came out so, so fine. I think that's one of the great things about jazz is that you don't have, you don't have to follow the letter on it. It comes out so great.
Vic was a kind of a legitimate guy?

Yeah, Vic was a strict technician. I mean, he did things that I just couldn't believe that could be possible. I remember one day I brought him a copy of Rhapsody in Blue, and it had just come out then. And Vic had never seen that tune. This was just an example of his musicianship. I've been trying to play the doing thing for over 30 years now, and I still haven't played the whole thing through. And I'm telling you, he stood there, he sat down with that copy, the original copy. I mean, nothing left out, and played it from cover to cover. Right before me there, he did leave a thing out. And believe me, that's something. That's the kind of... That's sight. That's sight, he played that thing note for note. That's the kind of a musician he was. Didn't miss a thing. How did he play in the band?

Well, Vic was really an exhibitionist at the piano. He was all over the piano all the time, and he always wanted to display his technique. And he never missed an opportunity to let people know how much he could do. But he had something to go on, because he could really do it. He really played a great... In fact, I wouldn't classify Vic as a real great jazz pianist, but he certainly was a great technician. Certainly had a wonderful technique.

Well, he played at the Little Club. He had a band up there. I don't know if he had Tony Papalia playing up there with him. I just don't remember the exact combination that he had up there. And then he played at the Sanga. That was one of the feature spots that he played in the days when the Sanga had stage shows. He was a great standby there. In fact, he did lots of solos on the stage. They let him do lots of solos. Yeah, he was one of the real fine piano players around here. Another fine piano player was Howard Tiff. He played at the Alphine Theatre quite some time. I took some lessons from Howard too. Howard was a real fine, legitimate piano player. He could play almost anything too. And there was another fellow by the name of Don Chase. Don Chase played piano at the same time as Vic did at the Sanga. Of course, Don was kind of lost with Vic up there because Don was just a sort of a second piano to Vic. But he was a great piano player in his own right.
Were these guys jazz musicians? Captain Chase?

Well, I guess they probably played with dance bands. Let's put it this way, that they played with dance bands. I wouldn't know what he would exactly call them real jazz musicians because as I said, they were more or less legitimate. Readers. But I guess they did play with dance bands. There was another fellow by the name of Wilson that used to play piano. I think he played at the Lowest State. I can't think of his first name now. But he was quite an accomplished musician himself.
So many of them, you learn new names every day. Yeah, that's just it.
